payload.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core without a big-bang rewrite: lock the black-box contract (SPEC plus a conformance suite over commands, hooks and record format), build sofar-core in Rust (hook handlers, event append, fold, digest/status render, statusline) behind the same CLI contract, integrate with TypeScript fallback, ship prebuilt per-platform binaries via npm, and prove it as its own benchmark arm; it ships only if no held-out lead margin shrinks (bench-refresh D19). After conformance parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

payload.because:
- Sofar runs on every tool call of every agent session. A native core gives near-zero hook start-up, fast folds over very large records (this repo's own is 9.7 MB), a single binary with no Node dependency for Codex/Cursor/OpenCode users, and headroom for many parallel agents.
- Measured 0.31 hooks are only ~0.75% of session time today, so the win is future scale and distribution rather than today's tokens. That is why it goes incrementally, and must pass the same benchmark gate as any other change.
- A conformance-first strangler port means neither implementation can drift from the SPEC.
payload.chose:
Adopt Rust for sofar's HOT PATH, incrementally, starting now. Ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15 ("yes do it").
SUPERSEDES, for the hot path only, the CLAUDE.md engineering conventions:
- "TypeScript strict mode; Node ≥18; ES modules";
- "Dependencies: … Nothing else without logging a Decision". Rust crates are limited to serde, serde_json and ulid until another Decision adds one.

Scope of `sofar-core`: hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end), atomic event append, fold, digest/status render, and statusline.

TypeScript keeps: the MCP server, `sofar drive`, init/doctor/review, and cloud commands.

The contract comes first: docs/SPEC.md plus a black-box conformance suite over commands, hook stdin/stdout, env and record bytes. It runs against BOTH implementations.

The schema rail holds: event payload types stay authored ONLY in packages/schema/src. Rust types are GENERATED from them, never hand-written. Projection templates keep one source of truth, and Rust output is verified byte-identical by golden tests.

Parity gate: 100% conformance, perf targets met, and a benchmark arm "sofar-rust-core" vs "sofar-ts" that shrinks no D19 lead margin.

Sequencing: r1-fixes waves 1–2 land in TypeScript now, and the Rust core must reach parity INCLUDING them. After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only, which stops the TypeScript port surface growing. Distribution: prebuilt per-platform binaries through npm optionalDependencies, with a TypeScript fallback.
payload.over:
- A big-bang rewrite now: it freezes waves 1–3, leaves round 2 unable to attribute gains, and means porting 27.6k engine lines and 34k test lines before anything is trustworthy.
- Staying TypeScript-only behind a measure-first gate: the run owner's point is that the port cost grows with every feature, and Codex CLI, Turborepo and Biome show the path is proven.
payload.rule: Hot-path event and projection behaviour is defined by docs/SPEC.md plus the conformance suite and must pass against both the TypeScript and Rust implementations; Rust schema types are generated from packages/schema/src, never hand-written.

plan.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core incrementally (rust-core D1): contract first, then sofar-core in Rust behind the same CLI and hook contract, integrated with TypeScript fallback, shipped as prebuilt binaries, and proven as its own benchmark arm that shrinks no held-out lead margin (bench-refresh D19). After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

Black-box conformance suite in the TS repo: runs an implementation binary against golden fixtures (real records including this repo's 9.7 MB log, calib and smoke cells, corrupt and unknown lines, concurrent appends) and compares stdout, exit codes and record bytes. Green on TypeScript first.
Perf baseline harness: hook p50/p95 cold start and fold/digest latency at 10, 100 and 1,000 initiatives and 1–10 MB records, TypeScript numbers recorded as the target to beat
Cargo workspace crates/sofar-core; schema codegen from packages/schema/src (no hand-written payload types); dependency list per D1
Event envelope and atomic O_APPEND append; unknown and corrupt lines skipped with a warning, never fatal, never rewritten
Fold to initiative state with conformance parity
Digest/status render byte-identical to the projection templates (golden tests), including the 10k char cap behaviour
Hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end) with conformance parity, including r1-fixes wave 1–2 behaviour
Statusline command parity
TS entry points and hook shims dispatch to sofar-core when present, with TypeScript fallback and an explicit override for debugging
Prebuilt binaries per platform (darwin arm64/x64, linux x64/arm64, win32 x64) via npm optionalDependencies, plus a CI build matrix
Gate green: 100% conformance on both implementations and perf targets beaten
Benchmark arm sofar-rust-core vs sofar-ts under a frozen addendum; must shrink no D19 lead margin
Release after benchmark evidence (never before, per bench-refresh D20)
Switch the rule: new hot-path features are Rust-only; decide whether to port the remaining TypeScript surfaces

payload.because: The 10k injection cap, every clip budget, the redaction and guard regexes and the canonical event bytes all decide observable output; a Rust core that used its own defaults would pass no golden test against the live 9.4 MB record and would fork events.jsonl bytes on identical events (the spurious-diff hazard SPEC §Event envelope exists to prevent). Reproducing JS semantics is cheap and mechanical; tolerating drift would make "same bytes from both implementations" (D1) unprovable.
payload.chose: Byte parity is defined against the TypeScript engine's JavaScript text semantics, inventoried in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins: lengths and clips in UTF-16 code units, JS non-unicode regex classes, JS whitespace class, ECMAScript number formatting in canonical JSON, Node path.relative/basename, Math.round half-up, millisecond ISO timestamps. docs/HOTPATH.md is the hand-written contract inventory the conformance suite (1.2) drives; SPEC gaps it lists (G1–G15) are resolved by SPEC edits or Decisions, never by letting the two implementations differ.
payload.over: Rust-native defaults (char/byte lengths, Unicode-aware regex classes, ryu number formatting) with SPEC amended to tolerate the drift between implementations.
payload.rule: Hot-path Rust code reproduces the JavaScript text semantics pinned in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins, never Rust defaults; a parity difference is fixed in Rust or ruled by a Decision, never absorbed by loosening the conformance suite.

payload.because: Masking needs no hot-path code change in either implementation, keeps the shape of every volatile field asserted (a malformed ulid or timestamp still fails), and ulid randomness would defeat an unseeded clock override anyway. Leaving session-start's time-gated lines out would drop the surface the 10k cap and preface composition depend on.
payload.chose: The conformance suite (1.2) masks volatile bytes BY SHAPE instead of injecting a clock: a run-minted ulid becomes <ULID> only when its time part falls in the run's window, a run-minted ISO timestamp becomes <TS>, the two relative-age labels (Nm/Nh/Nd ago, ~Nh/~Nd since) become <AGO>, scratch paths become <ROOT>/<HOME>. Fixture bytes are never masked. Goldens are recorded from the TypeScript reference only, and only after the fixture horizon (newest fixture event + the 1 h cold-resume gap) so the presence of time-gated lines cannot flip. Everything else is pinned by building the child's environment from nothing but PATH (scratch HOME, git identity, XDG dirs, peer registry, update cache, LANG, TZ). Chosen under autonomy while the run owner's O6 ruling is outstanding; a SOFAR_NOW override can still be added later and would only shrink the mask list.

Latest stable 1.98.1 (2026-09-03); skip 1.98.0 (vtable miscompile); local machine has 1.97.1. x86_64-apple-darwin is Tier 2 since 1.90; aarch64-pc-windows-msvc Tier 1 since 1.91 (so ship win32-arm64 too, beyond the 3.2 list). (1.96) in tests; integer format_into/NumBuffer (1.98) for allocation-free digest rendering; std::io::pipe (1.87) if drive ever moves to Rust. Ideas only — adopting any of these that touches D1's crate list needs a Decision.

Rust research 2/6 — HOT-PATH ARCHITECTURE ideas. (1) Synchronous hook binary, no tokio. Have `sofar init` write hooks in exec form pointing at the RESOLVED native binary, never the npm .bin Node shim: one Node start per tool call is the main latency (esbuild overwrites its shim for the same reason). (2) Plain appends = build the full line, one write_all on O_APPEND. Check-then-append (lazy session registration) = exclusive File::lock on a SIDECAR `events.jsonl.lock` (Windows: append-only handles cannot be locked and LockFileEx may be mandatory — never lock events.jsonl itself); TypeScript must take the same lock (coordinate with r1-fixes 1.2 idempotent registration); add an idempotency key so the fold dedupes if a writer bypasses the lock; test N parallel MIXED Rust/TS writers (the 1.2 concurrent case is a natural home). (3) Incremental fold via a checkpoint {schema_hash, byte_offset, last_line_hash, state}: fold only the tail, any mismatch → full refold, partial last line skipped with a warning (maps onto the existing .index cursor rules in HOTPATH §Derived index on the hot path). (4) Byte-identity traps already pinned by HOTPATH P1–P9 and the 1.2 unicode/append goldens: 10k cap in UTF-16 units (len_utf16), sort by UTF-16 code units, JS `1e+21` vs ryu `1e21`, key order, serde_json REJECTS lone surrogates that JS accepts (syn.unicode append step has one), toISOString ms format, never localeCompare/Intl.

Rust research 3/6 — SCHEMA CODEGEN (task 2.1). Pipeline proposal: ts-json-schema-generator 2.9 → committed JSON Schema → typify 0.8 run from an xtask (not build.rs) → generated crate COMMITTED, with a CI regen-diff check. Pin the codegen to the TypeScript 5.9/6 programmatic API: TypeScript 7.0 has no stable programmatic API until 7.1 (this repo is on TS 7 — typescript-7 record). typify's anyOf handling is weak, so a narrow purpose-built emitter over the 37 exported schema types may be simpler than typify. guards.ts validation is LOGIC, not a type: port it by hand and conformance-test it separately (syn.guards golden).

Rust research 4/6 — CRATES. D1 currently allows serde, serde_json, ulid only; each addition below needs a Decision citing D1. Suggested: serde_json 1.0.151 on the hook path; lexopt for the hook CLI (clap only for a human CLI, if ever); insta (goldens), proptest, cargo-fuzz (fold must never panic on corrupt lines); gungraun + hyperfine for perf gates (1.3 harness); cargo-nextest. Keep tantivy, rmcp, tokio OUT of the hook binary. Optional and conditional: sonic-rs for bulk fold (needs compile-time SIMD; baseline x86_64 loses it), rkyv only as a versioned derived cache, memmap2 only for logs above ~10 MB (SIGBUS on truncation).

Rust research 5/6 — BUILD AND DISTRIBUTION (Phase 3). Release profile lto=fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip. PGO later via cargo-pgo on a replay corpus (the 1.2 fixtures are that corpus). Static musl on Linux. Per-platform npm optionalDependencies with a JS resolver that falls back to TypeScript when the native package is missing (npm/cli#4828 is the known optionalDependencies install bug). Provide an env switch between cores from the first integration (Turborepo lesson; matches 3.1's "explicit override for debugging"). Commit a pass/fail snapshot of conformance per platform (oxc pattern).

Rust research 6/6 — CAPABILITY EDGES to evaluate later (ideas, no decision): (a) Claude Code `mcp_tool` hook type could route PostToolUse to the already-running MCP server with no process spawn at all (not SessionStart; Codex/Cursor would still spawn). (b) napi-rs v3 can compile the same Rust to WASM so the TypeScript FALLBACK is the same core — conformance by construction, no dual maintenance (would change 3.1's fallback design). (c) Hash-chained log (blake3 per line + previous hash) → tamper-evident record, cheap cache validation, "state as of event N"; a FORMAT change, needs a FORMAT.md/SPEC Decision. (d) Offline BM25 search over 1,000+ records (tantivy or SQLite FTS5), outside the hook binary. (e) WASI 0.3 sandboxed user plugins (custom guards/renderers).

Rust research verdicts (peer session, 2026-09-15) 1/3 — for the run owner's review; nothing adopted, decisions still needed before use. ADOPT (no material loss found): toolchain 1.98.1 pinned via rust-toolchain.toml (skip 1.98.0); edition 2024 with let chains, cfg_select!, assert_matches!, format_into (MSRV only affects source builders; binaries ship); synchronous one-shot hook binary, no tokio; byte-identity trap fixtures (already in the 1.2 suite: UTF-16 cap, sort, number format, key order, surrogates, ISO ms); env switch between cores from day one; release profile lto=fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip, with split debuginfo kept for crash triage; static musl Linux; dev-only crates insta, proptest, cargo-fuzz, nextest, gungraun + hyperfine (dev deps, still listed in the D1 amendment).

Rust research verdicts 2/3 — ADOPT WITH A CONDITION (real pain found). File locking: Node has no native flock, so a Rust-only File::lock cannot coordinate with TypeScript writers; use a protocol both can implement (exclusive-create sidecar lockfile via open 'wx'/O_EXCL with stale-lock recovery) plus the idempotency key in fold; File::lock only once TS writers are gone; network filesystems stay best-effort. Direct native hook command: absolute machine-specific binary paths in a committed .claude/settings.json break teammates, CI and upgrades (npm prefixes differ); mitigate with a tiny sh/.cmd resolver shim (a few ms vs ~40 ms Node) or write paths only to settings.local.json, and keep a working default when the binary is absent. Incremental fold checkpoint: events.jsonl is NOT byte-append-only in practice — git union merges across branches/worktrees reorder or insert lines, so byte_offset alone is unsafe; validate with prefix hash + line count + last-line hash, any mismatch → full refold, fuzz it. Schema codegen (D1 requires it): ts-json-schema-generator pinned to TS 5.9/6; spike typify, fall back to a narrow emitter if unions come out poorly. Per-platform npm binaries: CI matrix and release complexity, Windows antivirus false positives, supply-chain signing — required to ship Rust at all, keep the TS fallback resolver. Claude Code mcp_tool hooks (no spawn): Claude-only, not at SessionStart, and capture silently stops if the MCP server is disconnected or crashed — only for non-critical capture, with missed-event detection, proven by ablation before relying on it.

Rust research verdicts 3/3 — DEFER (cost > gain today): napi-rs WASM single core replacing the TS fallback (WASM instantiate cost, no WASI flock, harder debugging; spike after Phase 2 parity, potentially a big maintenance win); tantivy search (multi-MB binary, index upkeep; `sofar find` exists; only on measured need, never in the hook binary); rmcp Rust MCP server (after parity, task 4.3); rkyv cache; memmap2 (SIGBUS, records under 10 MB); mimalloc (unproven for ms-lived processes); PGO (5–15% of a tiny runtime); WASI plugins (no product need yet); win32-arm64 (add when CI is stable). REDESIGN BEFORE CONSIDERING: hash-chained log — a single linear chain breaks under sofar's normal git union merges of concurrent branches/worktrees (two branches append different events, the merge interleaves them, the chain is invalid), plus corrections, export/import and old readers; if tamper-evidence is wanted, design per-session chains or a verification-time Merkle digest over ULID-sorted lines; needs a FORMAT.md/SPEC Decision. DECLINE: sonic-rs (compile-time SIMD, unchecked-UB APIs, slower on aarch64; serde_json suffices below ~10 MB).

payload.because: The user pays per spawn, so the measurement must include process start and be runnable against any implementation binary; per-cell p50 and p95 is the smallest set that catches both a median regression and a tail regression at each scale; hardware differences dwarf the margins being gated.
payload.chose: The perf target for the Rust core is the checked-in TypeScript baseline (packages/engine/test/conformance/perf/baseline.typescript.json), recorded by the 1.3 runner with the same black-box method the conformance suite uses (one process per hook, spawn to exit, p50/p95 nearest rank over 20 spawns) across 10/100/1,000 initiatives × 1/10 MB bound logs, this repo's record and a no-record floor. The 3.3 gate (SOFAR_PERF_GATE=1) passes only when every candidate p50 AND p95 is ≤ the target in every cell, candidate and reference re-measured on the same machine in the same sitting.
payload.over: In-process micro-benchmarks of fold/render (would not count node boot, the part Rust removes, and cannot run against a binary); a single aggregate score (would let a 10 MB regression hide behind a 1 MB win); comparing against numbers recorded on another machine.
payload.rule: A Rust perf claim is made only with `npm run perf` numbers (SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN, same machine as a fresh reference run), never with in-process or hand-timed figures; the 3.3 gate is every cell's p50 and p95 at or under the recorded target.

payload.text: Hot-path perf: `npm run perf` (SOFAR_PERF=1 vitest --project perf, ~6 min, spawns ~1,200 processes) measures every hook, statusline and status at scale; `SOFAR_PERF_RECORD=1` re-records packages/engine/test/conformance/perf/baseline.typescript.json (+ .md), `SOFAR_PERF_CELLS=repo,floor` limits cells (merged into the baseline when recording), `SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN=<binary>` measures a candidate with ratios, `SOFAR_PERF_GATE=1` fails a candidate over the target. Results for non-record runs land in $TMPDIR/sofar-perf.<impl>.{json,md}. Skipped under plain `npm test`. Never run it with other CPU-heavy work in flight — the numbers are wall clock.

1.3 baseline findings (Apple M4 Pro, node 24.15, a79c4a7; docs/HOTPATH.md §Perf baseline has the table). Boot floor is 31 ms per hook (node 21 ms + stub + fast bundle) — what a native binary removes. Fold cost scales with EVENT COUNT not bytes: 13 ms for 3,595 events, ~220 ms for 35,903, 2.3 ms for session-driver's 789 long lines; renderStatus < 1 ms. Appending hooks fold twice (handler + regenerateProjections) → ~610 ms vs ~313 ms read-only at 10 MB; sharing one fold is the first structural win (applies to TS too). The 100 ms shim budget holds only to ~1 MB/4k events; 10 MB blows it 3–6×. 1,000 siblings add ~70 ms warm / ~125 ms cold to session-start (registration scan + index rebuild), < 10 ms to other hooks. Rust improvement ideas from this (D3 record): (1) one fold per process shared by append and projections; (2) a streaming line decoder that validates the envelope without materialising a JSON value per line (serde borrowed structs); (3) the derived index as the primary read path for session-start's sibling scan so 1,000 siblings cost a directory listing, not 1,000 opens.

payload.text: 2.1 codegen findings (D3 record). (1) ts-json-schema-generator 2.9.0 installs its own TypeScript 5.9.3 nested under node_modules/ts-json-schema-generator, so the TS 7 workspace compiler is untouched — no separate package needed. (2) Rooting the schema at `KnownEventPayloads` (type: 'KnownEventPayloads', expose: 'export', topRef: true) pulls all 20 payloads, 5 nested objects and 7 string enums transitively, so no type list exists to drift; a vitest test asserts the registry has 20 members each referencing a *Payload definition. (3) `jsDoc: 'basic'` does NOT apply `@asType` annotations — 'extended' is required; it also copies TS doc comments into the JSON Schema and thence into Rust `#[doc]`, which is desirable (docs flow one way). (4) TS `number` → JSON `number` → typify `f64`, which cannot derive Eq and mis-states the four integer fields (threshold_pct, context_window, max_sessions, tokens); fixed at the schema home with `@asType integer` JSDoc tags so they generate as i64. Deriving Eq on every generated type is now a guard: a future `number` field without the tag fails the build. (5) typify 0.8 generates `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none)]` for optional fields and no deny_unknown_fields (schema emitted with additionalProperties: true), matching the TypeScript validators that ignore unknown keys. (6) Validation rules (conditional requirements, integer ranges) are logic and cannot come from the type schema — they are hand-ported in sofar-core (2.2/2.3) and proven by the syn.corrupt golden's exact warning text. (7) typify's xtask compiles in ~20 s cold; the regen check `cargo xtask schema --check` runs under `npm test` only when cargo is on PATH.

payload.because: D2 lets a parity difference be ruled rather than absorbed; the WTF-8 type would cost every string operation in the core for an input no real writer produces (JSON.stringify emits `\ud800` only when a JS string already held a lone half). The conformance case that carries one (repo.append step 12) goes through the TypeScript-owned `event append` and renders through `status` with the same U+FFFD bytes. Revisit with a WTF-8 type only if a golden ever shows a re-serialized lone surrogate.
payload.chose: The Rust core's JSON layer (crates/sofar-core/src/json.rs) reproduces JSON.parse/JSON.stringify semantics (P5: ECMAScript number formatting, last-wins duplicate keys, integer-like keys first in property order, f64 for every number, non-finite → null) with ONE ruled divergence: a lone-surrogate `\uD800`–`\uDFFF` escape decodes to U+FFFD at parse time, because Rust strings are UTF-8 and cannot hold a lone surrogate. UTF-16 lengths and stdout bytes are identical to Node's (which also emits U+FFFD when writing a lone surrogate); the only observable difference is a lone surrogate RE-SERIALIZED to JSON by the Rust core (`�` raw instead of `\ud800`), which can happen only when hook stdin or a log line carries one and the core re-emits it into an index file, a hookSpecificOutput line, or a payload it mints.
payload.over: A WTF-8 string newtype threaded through the fold, digest and every text helper so lone surrogates survive a round trip byte-for-byte; or serde_json::Value (rejects lone surrogates outright, u64/i64 number model, BTreeMap key order).
payload.rule: A lone-surrogate JSON escape decodes to U+FFFD in the Rust core; every other JSON.parse/JSON.stringify behaviour (P5) is reproduced exactly and proven by fixture tests generated from Node.

TASK CHANGES: (1) generator PARAMETERISED and exported (initiatives, writers, events per stream, type mix, size distribution with the tail) so the cloud harness drives the same one; (2) report the fold-cost CURVE vs events and vs bytes and name the log size that crosses 100 ms (≥100 ms refold p95 decides cloud refold-per-batch vs snapshot+tail); (3) always report COLD PROCESS and WARM FOLD separately; (4) digest and statusline render cost as one record's sessions[] grows to 100 writers; (5) union-merge test must include N branches appending to the SAME initiative's events.jsonl, plus across-initiative merges. 2.2 Rust improvement ideas recorded per D3 (none built): (1) a WTF-8 string type would remove the one ruled divergence (D13, lone surrogates) — worth it only if a golden ever shows a re-serialized lone surrogate. (2) `Object::js_ordered` reproduces JS property order (array-index keys first); if 2.4 finds no output that depends on insertion order, the Vec-backed object could become a sorted map for faster lookups on wide payloads (plan_updated). (3) `write_number` goes through `format!("{:e}")` — a direct shortest-digits routine (Ryu-style, via `core::fmt::flt2dec` if it stabilises) would remove an allocation per number; measure under D5 before touching. (4) `File::lock`/`try_lock` (std 1.89) stays out until the TypeScript writer is gone (D9); the O_EXCL sidecar via `File::create_new` (1.77) is what both sides share. (5) `Option::is_none_or` (1.82) and let-chains (edition 2024) carried the presence/absence semantics cleanly; `[T]::as_chunks` (1.88) in sha256. (6) identity: 2 s subprocess wait polls try_wait at 1 ms; a pipe-read with a deadline on a helper thread would cut the granularity if the ~8 ms git spawn is ever attacked (needs its own Decision per D7/O3). (7) `format_into` (named in the 2.2 next action) is not a std method at 1.98.1 — `std::fmt::Write` on String is the tool; no change needed.

payload.text: 2.3 design notes and improvement ideas (D3). Rust docs consulted: releases.rs 1.96–1.98 — assert_matches! (1.96), integer format_into / NumBuffer, str::substr_range, String::from_utf16le_lossy (1.98); none changes the hot path today. Ideas recorded, not built: (i) `format_into` for the `line N:` warning prefixes and the counters in to_json would drop one String alloc per warning — measure under 1.5 before adopting; (ii) the guard matcher memoizes failed (token, unit) states in a HashSet per pattern per subject — a bitset sized tokens×units would be allocation-free for the common short subject; (iii) state→Json→text for the `fold` output allocates the whole Json tree; a direct writer (as serialize_event does) would halve the canonical-output cost, but `fold` is a conformance surface, not a hook, so it does not gate 3.3; (iv) the snapshot wire is JSON-shaped exactly like the TypeScript SnapshotWire (same keys, insertion order per interface) — byte parity with TS was NOT made a goal because TS key order in `sessions[]` depends on event order (keys appear when first assigned); if 3.1 ever wants Rust to read a TS-written snapshot, parse_snapshot already accepts it shape-wise but the version check ties a snapshot to one engine version, so cross-implementation reading is a decision for later, not a bug. Known non-parity outside the contract: `--take`/`--since` accept JS Number forms for decimal/exponent/whitespace but not hex (`0x10`) — commander+Number would; the runner passes plain integers. Guards: no regex crate (D9) — the glob is compiled to the regex's automaton over UTF-16 units, `.` excluding the four JS line terminators (P3), and the guards.test.ts assertions are ported verbatim plus code-unit and line-terminator cases.

Fold parity against the Rust core: `cargo build --release -p sofar-core && SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN="$PWD/target/release/sofar-core" npx vitest run fold-parity` (the runner splits the value on spaces, so use an absolute path with none; needs `npm run build` first for the reference in record mode only). The same eight cases run in-process with `cargo test -p sofar-core --test fold_parity`, which fails with a byte diff against golden/*.state.json. `npm run schema:emit` now runs BOTH emitters (fingerprint then Rust JSON Schema); a schema change means schema:emit, then `cargo xtask schema`, then a bumped snapshot version by construction (the fingerprint hash is baked at compile time via include_str!, the engine version via build.rs from packages/engine/package.json).

Peer sofar-r1-fixes-1c (2026-09-16, r1-fixes 2.5, D24 — commit to follow, post-RC release, NOT in 179b8fd which round 2 keeps measuring): three OPTIONAL fold outputs and one edge kind, additive, nothing renamed (D21), no golden changes. (1) `ran` edge gains attrs {ok, exit?, test?} ONLY when command_run carries `ok` (self-improve D2); `test` = the test-shaped shell segment per the closed recognizer in core/derived.ts (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun test, npx/bunx vitest|jest|mocha|ava|tap|pytest|rspec|phpunit|cypress run|playwright test|node --test, cargo/go/dotnet/swift/mix/gradle/mvn/make/deno/zig test; segments split on && || ; | newline, quote-aware, after VAR=value prefixes; clipped to 120 chars). (2) New edge kind `tested` (task → command:<event id>) for every task ACTIVE at a test-shaped command with a KNOWN `ok` — same window as `worked`; not in stateOf. (3) stateOf gains `sessions[].activity.failed?` (count of ok:false, absent when 0), `sessions[].activity.last_test?: {cmd, ok, exit?}`, `task_tests?: Record<taskId, {cmd, ok, exit?, ts, event_id}>` (absent when empty). Unknown `ok` is never a failure nor a test outcome. A record without `ok` folds byte-identically. Rust mirror: a follow-up to 2.3 once the r1-fixes commit lands and is merged here — port the recognizer (P3 regex semantics, quote-aware split) into fold.rs/edges_for_event + activity, extend GraphEdge attrs and SessionActivity/task_tests in to_json/from_json, and take the shared case (proposed id FP-09-command-outcomes-and-tests) into tests/fold_parity.rs. Not a 3.3 gate change: round 2 measures 179b8fd.

payload.text: Ideas from 2.5/2.6 (D3), none built: (1) every hook folds the bound log from scratch (fold_file) — the TypeScript engine caches per process only, so parity holds, but a per-record fold snapshot on disk (D14's versioned snapshot, keyed by log size+mtime like the index cursors) would make session-start/user-prompt O(new events) on the 9.7 MB record; measure under D5 at 1.5's corpus first. (2) refresh_guards and refresh_files each re-read graph.json/guards.json and re-run the pass; post-tool calls guards then (on a path hit) files, session-start calls both — one pass over both reducers would halve the meta reads. payload.because: Exit 64 is already the contract HOTPATH pins for "not mine" and D14 chose it precisely because the shim cannot know the colour ladder outcome; one env marker keeps both diagnostics for a human running sofar-core directly while the stub's fallback is the answer under dispatch. Sharing update-cache.ts between the stub and update-check.ts keeps one refresh policy, and the stub's cost is a file read only after a core-rendered statusline or status. The unfiltered run is the standalone 3.1 proof the plan asked for and is the shape the 3.3 gate and the 4.1 arm will use.
payload.chose: The boot stub (cli/boot.ts, rust-core 3.1) dispatches by exit code, not by re-parsing argv: every `event`, `statusline` and `status` argv is spawned on the native core with stdio inherited and `SOFAR_CORE_DISPATCHED=1`; the core's exit 64 (NotOurs, or a styled `status`) means "run the TypeScript CLI on the same argv" — the core reads no stdin before deciding and prints no exit-64 diagnostic when dispatched, so the fallback sees whole stdin and clean streams — and every other exit is mirrored. The core is `SOFAR_CORE=<path>` (`0`/empty forbids one), else the platform package `@sofar/core-<platform>-<arch>` resolved from the stub (the one constant 3.2 may rename); absent means TypeScript silently, a named core that cannot spawn warns once and falls back, a signal-killed core exits 1 (stdin gone, no fallback). The update-refresh claim moves to the stub after a core-rendered `statusline`/`status` (cli/update-cache.ts, node builtins only, shared with update-check.ts), keeping the O2 ruling that the binary only reads the cache; `sofar-core status` renders the stderr notice with the stderr caps ladder. Proof: the reference conformance suite with `SOFAR_CORE=$PWD/target/release/sofar-core` — 27/27 cases, no tag skipped, `event append`, styled `status` and `commit-trailer` reaching TypeScript through the stub's own fallback — plus a fake-core dispatch test under `npm test` and a negative control (a core that always exits 1 fails 25/27). The hook shims keep `exec sofar event <hook>`: a direct exec needs a stable per-machine binary path, which is the 3.2 install layout's to settle.
payload.over: The stub re-implementing the argv grammar (a third copy of parseRoot/dispatch) or the colour ladder to decide the styled-status case itself; capturing the core's stderr to hide the exit-64 diagnostics (changes the child's stderr TTY-ness, so a human at a terminal would get a plain notice where TypeScript colours it); the core claiming and spawning the refresh itself (O2, rejected); rewriting the shims to exec the binary now with an install path guessed ahead of 3.2.
payload.rule: The boot stub interprets exactly one core exit code, 64, as "TypeScript runs it"; the core never reads stdin or writes a byte before returning 64, and a new dispatched shape or a second interpreted exit needs a Decision citing this one.
